title: 2016-2023 Tacoma automatic: driveline vibration coasting or braking from 30 to 10 mph
summary: Toyota T-SB-0124-20 Rev1: a vibration in the seat, floor or steering wheel while slowing from 30 to 10 mph on 6-speed automatic Tacomas. Fix is a steering wheel damper, then measuring the rear pinion joint angle and, if it's out of spec, new rear leaf springs.

specs.name: Speed range
specs.value: 30 down to 10 mph, coasting or braking

specs.name: Joint angle
specs.value: Pinion flange angle minus propeller shaft angle

specs.name: Labor
specs.value: 1.1 hr damper and joint angle; plus 1.0 hr to R&R leaf springs

steps.text: Doesn't apply to manual-transmission trucks (don't use these springs on them), trucks with a lift or leveling kit, or 4WD TRD Off-Road trucks built after the 2016 production change VINs listed in the bulletin.

Confirm the vibration slowing from 30 to 10 mph. 4WD: remove the rear driveshaft, shift to 4WD HI and test drive; if it still vibrates, the bulletin doesn't apply. 2WD: shift to neutral while slowing; if the vibration doesn't change, the bulletin doesn't apply.

Disconnect the battery negative and wait at least 90 seconds, remove the steering wheel pad, and install the damper with two new screws at 2.35 N·m (20.8 in-lbf). Keep the switch and airbag wiring clear and reinstall the pad.
Put the truck on a drive-on lift or alignment rack so the suspension is at ride height.

With the digital angle gauge in absolute mode and its screen facing the passenger side, measure the pinion flange angle (small-flange trucks need the propeller shaft off first) and the angle of the rear section of the propeller shaft.

Joint angle = pinion flange angle minus propeller shaft angle; it can be negative. Note whether the truck has firm-ride suspension (option codes CW, OF, OC, PT or PY) and its model code from the door jamb label, then compare with Table 2 in the bulletin.

In spec: test drive 10-30 mph and confirm it's better. Out of spec: replace the rear leaf springs, U-bolt nuts at 60 N·m (44 ft-lbf), with shock and spring-bushing fasteners final-torqued on the ground. Test drive again.

body: The joint-angle spec table (Table 2) is split by drivetrain, model code, cab, grade and suspension, and its layout doesn't survive text extraction cleanly, so the ranges aren't copied here. Read them from page 15 of the bulletin.
